strengths: Well-motivated paradigm shift from noise-to-data to data-to-data generation for video inpainting, addressing real limitations of existing diffusion-based approaches
Technically sound VP-SDE bridge formulation with rigorous velocity-matching objective (Eq. 11-12) and proper mathematical grounding
Novel Adaptive Mask Modulation (AMM) strategy provides practical solution to balance background fidelity with generative flexibility for varying occlusion sizes
Strong qualitative results demonstrating superior texture quality and temporal consistency; interesting emergent property of implicit shadow removal without explicit supervision
Thoughtful dataset construction combining synthetic (ROSE) and 31,000 real-world composite samples with distribution bias mitigation
Clear presentation with well-structured methodology, proper algorithms, and good visual comparisons across diverse scenarios
weaknesses: Critical absence of quantitative evaluation: no LPIPS, SSIM, FVD, or temporal consistency metrics provided, making rigorous validation impossible and enabling potential selection bias in qualitative examples
No ablation studies validating key design choices: AMM necessity, VP-SDE vs. Brownian Bridge, dual conditioning benefits, variance schedule sensitivity, or component contributions to improvements
Limited technical novelty: primarily applies existing bridge model techniques (Zhou et al., 2023a; Chen et al., 2023) to new domain; AMM is relatively simple element-wise modulation
Incomplete experimental scope: no user studies, failure case analysis, computational efficiency comparison, performance across object scales, or systematic resolution sensitivity analysis

Reproducibility concerns: no code release, vague SAM2/Qwen3-VL filtering details, unjustified hyperparameters (β_min=0.01, β_max=50.0, 1000 timesteps, 50 inference steps), missing variance schedule specification and architecture modifications

Mathematical clarity gaps: guidance term h(z_t,t,z_src) tractability claimed but not proven; relationship between β(t) and σ_t scheduling unclear; AMM's mathematical interaction with bridge dynamics not analyzed
Lack of failure mode discussion: while paper acknowledges strong priors hinder large object removal, no empirical validation, systematic analysis, or discussion of when/why this occurs

strengths: Well-motivated reformulation from noise-to-data to data-to-data generation with clear intuition for video object removal domain
Rigorous mathematical foundation with proper derivation of VP-SDE bridge marginal distribution, analytical guidance term, and equivalence proofs to score matching

Comprehensive experimental evaluation including new BridgeRemoval-Bench benchmark (150 videos), 6 baseline comparisons, user study with 1,440 evaluations, and multiple metrics addressing both object removal and background preservation
Strong empirical results with 1.64 dB PSNR improvement on proposed benchmark and consistent best or second-best performance across all quantitative metrics
Practical solution to bridge-prior rigidity trade-off via Adaptive Mask Modulation that enables effective removal of objects across scales
Clear algorithmic presentation with detailed pseudo-code, good figures, and thorough ablation studies on key components
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: primarily applies established bridge theory (DDBM) to video inpainting domain; AMM is essentially standard FiLM conditioning applied to mask features
Adaptive Mask Modulation insufficiently explored: no comparative ablations against alternative modulation strategies; sensitivity to design choices and hyperparameters not analyzed
Incomplete ablation studies: missing investigation of dual-role of zsrc, variance schedule sensitivity, VAE/text encoder choices, and alternative conditioning mechanisms

Limited failure mode analysis: fast-moving objects acknowledged but not systematically investigated; no principled solutions proposed; missing statistics on failure frequency and other failure taxonomy

Evaluation methodology concerns: CLIP metrics as proxies not thoroughly validated; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals despite small metric differences; user study with modest sample size (24 participants)
Generalization questions: all experiments use single backbone (Wan2.1-1.3B); no cross-architecture validation; unclear how method-specific design choices are to this architecture

Training data analysis sparse: no ablation decomposing contribution of synthetic vs. real-world data; distribution characteristics of combined dataset not characterized; potential dataset biases unaddressed
Inference efficiency trade-off unexplained: 50% slower than ROSE baseline; no discussion of computational cost drivers or fine-grained inference speed analysis
Reproducibility gaps: project page URL incomplete; code release not mentioned; dataset sourcing details missing (especially TikTok permissions); Qwen3-VL filtering criteria not specified
Technical details under-explored: hyperparameter choices (variance schedule β values, learning rate) not justified; VAE latent quantization effects not discussed; sensitivity analysis absent
